minutes.headline: Board approved the Water District's earth removal permit and authorized Casella recycling renegotiation capped per ton
minutes.summary: The Select Board held an earth removal hearing for the Water District's new headquarters site and approved the permit with added conditions. It appointed two cable committee members, sent a support letter for the open space plan, renewed licenses (one contingent on taxes), and heard about a Chapter 61B conversion it likely cannot act on in time. It authorized the town manager to renegotiate the Casella contract because recycling will now cost the town, and planned workshops on town buildings.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved the Water District's earth removal permit with the Planning Director's conditions plus set hours of operation and warning signs.
The board authorized the town manager to renegotiate the Casella contract, with a cap per ton, because recycling will now cost the town.
Annual 2019 license renewals were approved, with all of one licensee's tavern licenses made contingent on payment of outstanding taxes.
The board agreed to send a letter of support for the open space and recreation plan and appointed two members to the cable committee.
A Chapter 61B land conversion was set for the January 8 agenda; the board is unlikely to exercise its right of first refusal.

why_it_matters: Recycling moves from a service the town was paid for to a per-ton cost, and that cost lands on the general fund, which is mostly funded by taxes.
The Water District permit lets excess fill leave the headquarters site under conditions on hours and signage, which affects truck traffic on nearby roads.
License fees have not been raised since 1995, so any increase the board takes up would change what local license holders pay.
watch_next: January 8 Select Board agenda: the Chapter 61B conversion and the board's first-refusal decision.
January 15 workshop with historical groups on town buildings; January 29 is held in reserve.
